**FITCHBURG CITY CLERK**
*Nov 24 2026 1:56 pm*

# October 27, 2026 10:05 a.m. - Monthly Retirement Board Meeting

The regular meeting of the Fitchburg Retirement Board was called to order by Chairperson Thomas Dateo Jr. on October 27, 2026, at 10:05 a.m., in the West Meeting Room of Fitchburg City Hall, located at 718 Main Street, Fitchburg, MA 01420.

Fitchburg Retirement Board members present: Thomas Dateo Jr. (Chair), Mary Cringan, Jacquelyn Cronin and Anna Farrell.

Fitchburg Retirement Board members absent: John Brown

Staff present: Director Steffani Santiago and Assistant Director Geraldine Conley.

### Review and Approval of the Retiree Payroll Warrant:

The Board reviewed the September 2026 Retiree Payroll Warrant totaling $1,926,468.17. On a motion made by Mary Cringan and seconded by Jacquelyn Cronin, to approve the September 2026 Retiree Payroll Warrant. Voted unanimously (4-0).

### Review and Approval of the Cash Disbursements Warrant:

The Board reviewed the October 2026 Cash Disbursements Warrant totaling $18,002.49. On a motion made by Anna Farrell and seconded by Mary Cringan, to approve the October 2026 Cash Disbursements Warrant. Voted unanimously (4-0).

### Review and Approval of the Refunds/Rollovers/Transfers Warrant:

The Board reviewed the October 2026 Refunds/Rollovers/Transfers Warrant totaling $113,419.86. On a motion made by Jacquelyn Cronin and seconded by Anna Farrell, to approve the October 2026 Refunds/Rollovers/Transfers Warrant. Voted unanimously (4-0).

### Review and Approve Meeting Minutes:

The Board reviewed the September 22, 2026 meeting minutes. On a motion made by Mary Cringan and seconded by Jacquelyn Cronin, to approve the September 22, 2026 Meeting Minutes. Voted unanimously (4 -0).

### Michael K. Smith ADR Application Update:

Ms. Santiago informed the board that she sent notification to Mr. Smith including the findings of the Medical Panel for an Ordinary Disability Retirement as well as his right to a hearing. Mr. Smith will attend the November 24, 2026 Board Meeting.

### Director/Assistant Director Communications (Pending/Tabled Matters):

- Patrick J. Roy Option D Update - Ms. Santiago advised the Board that Meagan Roy was appointed Personal Representative of Mr. Roy's Estate and that the City would be issuing Mr. Roy's final pay in November. Ms. Santiago advised the Board; she would then recalculate the Option D benefit and retro accordingly.
- Employer ID Number - The Board reviewed the email correspondence from Attorney Gibson relative to the retirement system obtaining its own TIN from the IRS as recommend by PERAC's legal counsel Ice Miller. Ms. Santiago and Ms. Cronin expressed concerns relative to how staff payroll would be processed and whether this would present year-end issues for 1099 filings. Ms. Santiago advised the Board that she had contacted the Leominster and Gardner Directors to inquire what, if any action they have taken. The Board agreed to hold the matter until the new year.
- 1099 Distribution via Bay State/PostGrid - Ms. Santiago informed the Board that Bay State was offering clients the ability to utilize their service contract with PostGrid to automate the distribution of the System's CY26 1099-R this year. Ms. Santiago reviewed the software platform/cost and advised that two other Bay State clients had utilized the service last year for 1099 distributions and would be doing so again this year. Ms. Santiago advised between the cost to purchase blank tax forms and envelopes, the cost of postage, and the time it would require staff to prepare the mailings, the Board would be saving money by automating the mailing as the projected quote was approximately $1.00 per mailing including postage. The Board discussed the option and agreed that it is worth trying out.
- Ex-Officio Member Update - Ms. Cronin notified City administration over six months ago of her intent to retire. The city only recently advertised the Auditor job posting. The Board reviewed and discussed Attorney Gibson's email concerning the Ex-Officio Member position potential vacancy. Ms. Cronin confirmed that someone would have to be assigned the duties and responsibilities of the Auditor upon her retirement and that person would serve as the Ex-Officio Member until the position was filled permanently.
- Fall 2026 Newsletter - Ms. Santiago added two pages to the newsletter as suggested by Minuteman Press. The file newsletter has been sent to Minuteman Press for printing and distribution. All active and retired members will receive a copy via U.S. Postal service and there will be copies available in the Retirement Office.
- City Benefits Administration - Ms. Santiago advised the Board that the City's Payroll Manager position had been vacant since June 2026. The City's Benefits Coordinator and Treasurer had been sharing the responsibility of processing the City's payrolls since. As a result, there has been a disruption in benefits administration for members and the Retirement Office has seen an increase in calls and walk-ins from our retirees and MTRS retirees seeking assistance with benefit related matters. The Board inquired why the city had not filled the payroll position. The Board asked if the Director had spoken with City administration and she advised that she had repeatedly to no avail. Ms. Santiago explained that the Treasurer had expressed sympathy and explained that payroll was the priority; which the Board understood. As Ms. Conley previously held the city's Benefits Coordinator position, the Retirement Office has done their best to assist the city, our members, and MTRS members in the interim. Mr. Dateo noted the Board had considered hiring a part-time employee and inquired whether the Board should consider hiring a full-time employee and taking over the benefit administration for the city's retirees. Mr. Dateo noted the Board would require the city to compensate the employee for the hours worked related to benefit administration. Ms. Santiago advised the board that she was aware of two other Board's in the Commonwealth who provided administrative services on the city's for retiree benefits, but that it was not common. She advised that she would contact the two Board Directors to gather more information. Ms. Cronin and Ms. Farrell both suggested the Board draft a letter to the Mayor and City Counsel expressing concerns about the Treasurer's office being short staffed and members not being able to get assistance concerning benefits. - Tabled to November 24, 2026 meeting.
